rows.solution:
The reaction as written has iron oxidised and silver deposited, so IRON is the anode and SILVER the cathode.

\(E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{\circ}_{\text{anode}} = (+0{\cdot}80) - (-0{\cdot}44)\)

\(E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = 1{\cdot}24\ \mathrm{V}\)

The commonest error here is to DOUBLE the silver value because two silver ions appear in the balanced equation. That is wrong: an electrode potential is an INTENSIVE property, a property of the half-cell itself, and multiplying a half-reaction through changes neither it nor the cell potential. The stoichiometric coefficient enters only through \(n\) in \(\Delta G = -nFE\), never into \(E^{\circ}\) itself.

Doubling it would have given \(1{\cdot}60 + 0{\cdot}44\); the distractor at \(2{\cdot}04\) V is built that way.

rows.stem: A first order reaction takes 30 minutes for 50% completion. The value of rate constant k would be :
rows.solution:
For a FIRST ORDER reaction the half-life is related to the rate constant by
\(t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0{\cdot}693}{k}\)

"50% completion in 30 minutes" IS the half-life, so
\(k = \dfrac{0{\cdot}693}{30} = 0{\cdot}0231\ \mathrm{min^{-1}} = 2{\cdot}31 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{min^{-1}}\)

[NONE of the four options carries this value. The nearest, \(2{\cdot}31 \times 10^{-3}\), has the right digits but is a factor of ten too small — as are all four, which sit between \(10^{-4}\) and \(10^{-3}\) where the answer is of order \(10^{-2}\). The marking scheme records the defect and instructs examiners to award full marks FOR ANY OPTION. Work the arithmetic, not the options.]

The unit is a check on the working: a first order constant must come out as reciprocal time, and reciprocal minutes is what dividing a pure number by 30 minutes gives.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : \(\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_2NH}\) is more basic than \(\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_3N}\) in aqueous solution.
Reason (R) : In \(\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_2NH}\), there is more steric hindrance and +I effect than \(\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_3N}\).
rows.context: For Questions number 15 to 18, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The Assertion is TRUE, but the Reason is FALSE.

Diethylamine IS the stronger base in aqueous solution — the observed order for ethylamines in water is secondary, then primary, then tertiary.

But the Reason describes diethylamine wrongly on BOTH counts. It has LESS steric hindrance than triethylamine, not more — two ethyl groups against three. And it has a SMALLER \(+\mathrm{I}\) effect, since the inductive push grows with the number of alkyl groups.

The real explanation is that the two effects PULL OPPOSITE WAYS in water. The \(+\mathrm{I}\) effect favours the tertiary amine by making the lone pair more available; but the cation formed on protonation must be STABILISED BY HYDROGEN BONDING to the surrounding water, and that needs hydrogens on the nitrogen — the tertiary amine's cation has only one, and its three ethyl groups crowd the water away besides.

The secondary amine is the compromise that wins, and it wins precisely BECAUSE it has less hindrance, which is the opposite of what the Reason says.

rows.subtopic: Definitions of Some Important Terms Pertaining to Coordination Compounds
rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : EDTA is used to determine hardness of water.
Reason (R) : EDTA is a bidentate ligand.
rows.context: For Questions number 15 to 18, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The Assertion is TRUE, but the Reason is FALSE.

EDTA IS used to determine the hardness of water — the calcium and magnesium ions responsible for hardness are titrated against a standard EDTA solution, with which they form 1:1 complexes.

But EDTA is HEXADENTATE, not bidentate. Count its donor atoms: two nitrogens, and one oxygen from each of four carboxylate arms — SIX in all, and it binds the metal through every one of them at once, wrapping right around the ion.

That is exactly why the method works. Wrapping around closes FIVE chelate rings, and the resulting complex is so exceptionally stable and so cleanly 1:1 that the titration has a sharp end point. A bidentate ligand would form a far weaker complex and a less reliable one.

Corrected to hexadentate, the Reason would have explained the Assertion well.

rows.subtopic: Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass
rows.stem:
A solution is prepared by dissolving 10 g of non-volatile solute in 200 g of water. It has a vapour pressure of \(31{\cdot}84\) mm Hg at 308 K. Calculate the molar mass of the solute.
(Vapour pressure of pure water at 308 K = 32 mm Hg)
rows.solution:
Raoult's law for a non-volatile solute relates the relative lowering of vapour pressure to the mole fraction of the solute, which for a dilute solution may be taken as the mole RATIO:
\(\dfrac{p^{\,\circ} - p_s}{p^{\,\circ}} = \dfrac{w_B/M_B}{w_A/M_A}\)

Substituting — 10 g of solute in 200 g of water, of molar mass 18:
\(\dfrac{32 - 31{\cdot}84}{32} = \dfrac{10/M_B}{200/18}\)
\(\dfrac{0{\cdot}16}{32} = \dfrac{10}{M_B} \times \dfrac{18}{200}\)
\(0{\cdot}005 = \dfrac{0{\cdot}9}{M_B}\)

\(M_B = \dfrac{0{\cdot}9}{0{\cdot}005} = 180\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\)

The answer is worth recognising: 180 g per mole is the molar mass of GLUCOSE, the commonest non-volatile solute in problems of this kind.

Note how small the lowering is — 0.16 mm Hg out of 32, half of one per cent — which is what makes this measurement demanding in practice and why osmotic pressure is preferred for macromolecules.

rows.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
rows.stem:
How would you account for :
(a) The \(\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\) value for the \(\mathrm{Mn^{3+}/Mn^{2+}}\) couple is much more positive than that for \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}/Cr^{2+}}\) couple or \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}\) couple.
(b) Complete the following equation :
\(2\mathrm{MnO_4^{-}} + 16\mathrm{H^{+}} + 5\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}} \longrightarrow\)
rows.solution:
(a) Because reducing \(\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}\) produces a specially stable ion while reducing the other two does not.

\(\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}\) is \(3d^4\), and gaining one electron gives \(\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\), which is the exactly HALF-FILLED \(3d^5\) — an arrangement of considerable extra stability. Manganese(III) therefore takes an electron very readily, and a large POSITIVE potential is what that means.

\(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) is \(3d^3\), which in an octahedral aqueous environment is the stable half-filled \(t_{2g}^3\) arrangement — already settled, with little inclination to be reduced. And \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\) is itself the half-filled \(3d^5\), so reducing IT would destroy a stable configuration rather than create one.

In each case it is the stability of the ion being REACHED that decides, and only manganese gains by the change.

(b) Permanganate oxidises oxalate to carbon dioxide in acid, manganese falling from \(+7\) to \(+2\):
\(2\mathrm{MnO_4^-} + 16\mathrm{H^+} + 5\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Mn^{2+}} + 10\mathrm{CO_2} + 8\mathrm{H_2O}\)

Ten electrons change hands: two permanganates take five each, and five oxalates give up two each as carbon rises from \(+3\) to \(+4\). Note that each oxalate yields TWO molecules of carbon dioxide, which is where the 10 comes from.

The reaction is AUTOCATALYTIC — the \(\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\) produced speeds it up — which is why the first drop of permanganate decolourises slowly in a titration and the rest quickly.

rows.stem:
Predict the products of the following reactions :
(i) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Cu/273\,K}}\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2\,(aq)}}\)
rows.solution:
(i) Copper at 273 K does NOTHING to ethanol — no reaction occurs at that temperature.

The dehydrogenation of an alcohol over copper requires about 573 K. At that temperature a PRIMARY alcohol loses two hydrogens, one from the oxygen and one from the carbinol carbon, and gives an ALDEHYDE:
\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} \xrightarrow[573\ \mathrm{K}]{\mathrm{Cu}} \mathrm{CH_3CHO} + \mathrm{H_2}\)

[The temperature as printed, 273 K, is the freezing point of water and far too low for the reaction; the marking scheme accepts either "no reaction at 273 K" or the 573 K product, so the intended answer is ethanal.]

(ii) Phenol with AQUEOUS bromine gives 2,4,6-TRIBROMOPHENOL, as a white precipitate:
\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH} + 3\mathrm{Br_2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_2Br_3OH} + 3\mathrm{HBr}\)

All three available positions are substituted at once and no catalyst is needed: water lets the phenol ionise to phenoxide, which is so strongly activating that even the feeble electrophile in bromine water suffices.

rows.stem:
Give reasons for the following :
(i) p-nitrophenol is more acidic than p-methylphenol.
(ii) \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C - Br}\) on reaction with \(\mathrm{NaOCH_3}\) gives alkene as the main product and not an ether.
rows.solution:
(i) Because the two substituents pull in OPPOSITE directions, and acidity is decided by what they do to the PHENOXIDE ion.

The NITRO group is strongly electron WITHDRAWING, both inductively and — from the PARA position — by resonance, so it can take the anion's negative charge right onto its own oxygen. That stabilises the anion, and a more stable anion means the proton leaves more readily.

The METHYL group does the reverse: it RELEASES electron density into the ring, concentrating the charge on the anion and destabilising it.

So p-nitrophenol is the stronger acid by a wide margin — \(\mathrm{pK_a}\) about 7.1 against p-cresol's 10.2, and even phenol's own 10 sits between them.

(ii) Because sodium methoxide is a STRONG BASE as well as a good nucleophile, and the substrate is TERTIARY.

An ether would require SUBSTITUTION, and Williamson's synthesis proceeds by \(\mathrm{S_N}2\) — which needs the nucleophile to reach the carbon from behind. 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane's carbon is surrounded by three methyl groups and is effectively unreachable.

With substitution blocked, the methoxide's basicity takes over: it removes a \(\beta\) HYDROGEN instead, and the bromide leaves with it. The product is 2-METHYLPROPENE.

The way to make this ether is to reverse the roles — use METHYL bromide as the halide and sodium tert-butoxide as the alkoxide, so the alkoxide attacks a primary carbon where \(\mathrm{S_N}2\) works cleanly.

rows.stem: Define denaturation of protein. What is the effect of denaturation on the structure of protein ?
rows.solution:
DENATURATION is the process in which a protein, subjected to a physical change such as heating or a chemical change such as a change in pH, LOSES ITS BIOLOGICAL ACTIVITY.

EFFECT ON THE STRUCTURE. The weak forces that hold the chain in its native shape — hydrogen bonds, disulphide bridges and other interactions — are disrupted, so the helix uncoils and the globule unfolds.

The SECONDARY and TERTIARY structures are therefore DESTROYED, while the PRIMARY structure — the sequence of amino acid residues — REMAINS INTACT, because no peptide bond is broken.

The everyday instance is the coagulation of egg white on boiling: soluble globular albumin becomes an insoluble solid, and the change is irreversible. Curdling of milk is another.

rows.subtopic: Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass
rows.stem:
Give reason :
(a) Measurement of osmotic pressure method is preferred for the determination of molar masses of macromolecules such as proteins and polymers.
(b) Aquatic animals are more comfortable in cold water than in warm water.
(c) Elevation of boiling point of 1 M KCl solution is nearly double than that of 1 M sugar solution.
rows.solution:
(a) Because osmotic pressure is the one colligative property LARGE ENOUGH TO MEASURE for such a solute, and it is measured under conditions that do not harm it.

A macromolecule has an enormous molar mass, so even a substantial mass of protein or polymer dissolves to give very few moles, and every colligative effect is correspondingly tiny — the freezing point depression would be a few thousandths of a degree, below what a thermometer can read reliably.

Osmotic pressure is the exception on three counts. Its MAGNITUDE is large even for a very dilute solution. It is measured at ROOM TEMPERATURE, so the protein is not heated and does not denature, which the boiling point method would risk. And it uses MOLARITY rather than molality, which is the concentration a laboratory can prepare directly.

(b) Because the SOLUBILITY OF OXYGEN in water is HIGHER at a LOWER temperature.

Dissolving a gas is an exothermic process, so by Le Chatelier's principle warming drives it backwards. Cold water therefore holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water at the same pressure, and aquatic animals, which breathe what is dissolved, are the better off for it.

This is why thermal pollution — warm water discharged from a power station into a river — threatens fish without adding anything toxic at all.

(c) Because potassium chloride DISSOCIATES and sugar does not.

Elevation of boiling point is a colligative property: it counts PARTICLES, not formula units. Potassium chloride is a strong electrolyte and gives two ions from each formula unit, so its van't Hoff factor is \(i = 2\); sugar dissolves as whole molecules, so \(i = 1\).

Two equimolar solutions therefore hold TWICE as many particles in the salt solution as in the sugar one, and the elevation is about twice as great.

rows.stem:
Complete the following reactions :
(a) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2Br} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{Alc. KOH}} \mathrm{(A)} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HBr}} \mathrm{(B)}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{(A)} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{SOCl_2}} \mathrm{(B)}\)
and from (B) : \(\mathrm{(B)} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Na/Ether}} \mathrm{(C)}\) , \(\mathrm{(B)} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaOCH_3}} \text{2-Methoxypropane}\)
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE — part (b) is printed as a BRANCHED two-dimensional scheme: (A) --SOCl2--> (B), and from (B) two arrows FAN OUT, the upper one labelled Na/Ether to (C) and the lower one labelled NaOCH3 to 2-Methoxypropane. The linear transcription above splits that fan into two separate arrows from (B); it is faithful and loses no reagent, product or label, but it is not what the page looks like, so the real crop is worth attaching. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
(a) Alcoholic potassium hydroxide ELIMINATES, giving the alkene:
\(\mathrm{A} = \mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CH_2}\), propene

Adding hydrogen bromide back follows MARKOVNIKOV'S RULE — the proton goes to the carbon carrying more hydrogens, so the bromine goes to the MIDDLE carbon:
\(\mathrm{B} = \mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_3}\), 2-bromopropane

Note that the bromine has MOVED: it started on carbon 1 and ends on carbon 2. Eliminating and re-adding is the standard way of shifting a halogen along a chain.

(b) Work backwards from the named product. 2-Methoxypropane, \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}O{-}CH_3}\), comes from sodium methoxide attacking an isopropyl halide, so:
\(\mathrm{B} = \mathrm{CH_3CH(Cl)CH_3}\), 2-chloropropane

Thionyl chloride makes a chloride from an ALCOHOL, so:
\(\mathrm{A} = \mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3}\), propan-2-ol

Sodium in dry ether couples two molecules of the halide end to end — the Wurtz reaction:
\(\mathrm{C} = \mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}CH(CH_3)_2}\), 2,3-dimethylbutane

The same halide therefore gives an ether with an alkoxide and an alkane with sodium, which is a useful contrast: one reagent substitutes, the other couples.

rows.stem:
How do you convert the following : (Any three)
(a) Phenol to 2-Hydroxybenzaldehyde
(b) Anisole to 2-Methoxyacetophenone
(c) Propene to Propan-2-ol
(d) Ethanol to Ethanal
rows.solution:
(a) PHENOL TO 2-HYDROXYBENZALDEHYDE — the REIMER-TIEMANN reaction. Chloroform with aqueous alkali generates dichlorocarbene, which attacks the phenoxide ion at its ORTHO position; acidification then frees the aldehyde:
\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH} \xrightarrow[2.\ \mathrm{H^+}]{1.\ \mathrm{CHCl_3} + \text{aq. }\mathrm{NaOH}} \mathrm{o\text{-}HO{-}C_6H_4{-}CHO}\)

(b) ANISOLE TO 2-METHOXYACETOPHENONE — a Friedel-Crafts ACYLATION. The methoxy group is activating and ortho, para directing, and the ORTHO product is the one named:
\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OCH_3} + \mathrm{CH_3COCl} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. }\mathrm{AlCl_3}} \mathrm{o\text{-}CH_3O{-}C_6H_4{-}COCH_3}\)

(c) PROPENE TO PROPAN-2-OL — acid-catalysed hydration, following Markovnikov's rule so the hydroxyl lands on the MIDDLE carbon:
\(\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{H_2O} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+}} \mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3}\)
Hydroboration-oxidation would have given propan-1-ol instead.

(d) ETHANOL TO ETHANAL — oxidation of a primary alcohol with a MILD reagent that stops at the aldehyde:
\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{PCC}} \mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)
A stronger oxidising agent would carry the oxidation on to ethanoic acid; copper at 573 K achieves the same conversion by dehydrogenation.

rows.stem:
(i) State Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions. Write an expression for the molar conductivity of acetic acid at infinite dilution according to Kohlrausch's law.
(ii) Calculate the maximum work and \(\log \mathrm{K_c}\) for the given reaction at 298 K :
\(\mathrm{Ni\,(s)} + 2\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\,\mathrm{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\,\mathrm{(aq)} + 2\mathrm{Ag\,(s)}\)
Given : \(\mathrm{E}^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}/\mathrm{Ni}} = -\,0{\cdot}25\) V, \(\mathrm{E}^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Ag}^{+}/\mathrm{Ag}} = +\,0{\cdot}80\) V
1 F = 96500 C \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\)
rows.solution:
(i) KOHLRAUSCH'S LAW OF INDEPENDENT MIGRATION OF IONS states that the LIMITING molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the SUM of the individual contributions of its cation and its anion, each counted as often as the formula unit provides it.

At infinite dilution the ions are so far apart that each moves entirely INDEPENDENTLY of the other, which is what makes the simple sum valid.

For ACETIC ACID, which gives one \(\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}\) and one \(\mathrm{H^+}\):
\(\Lambda_m^{\circ}(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}) = \lambda^{\circ}_{\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}} + \lambda^{\circ}_{\mathrm{H^+}}\)

The law matters most for a WEAK electrolyte like this one, whose \(\Lambda_m^{\circ}\) cannot be found by extrapolating a plot — its molar conductivity rises too steeply near zero concentration for the extrapolation to be reliable. Kohlrausch's law lets it be assembled from ionic values measured on strong electrolytes instead.

(ii) Silver has the more positive potential, so it is the cathode and nickel the anode:
\(E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{\circ}_{\text{anode}} = 0{\cdot}80 - (-0{\cdot}25) = 1{\cdot}05\ \mathrm{V}\)

Nickel goes from 0 to \(+2\), so TWO electrons are transferred and \(n = 2\).

MAXIMUM WORK. The maximum work obtainable from a cell is the decrease in free energy:
\(w_{\max} = -\Delta_r G^{\circ} = nFE^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = 2 \times 96500 \times 1{\cdot}05\)
\(w_{\max} = 202650\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}\), that is \(202{\cdot}65\) kJ \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\)

Note the SIGN. \(\Delta_r G^{\circ}\) is \(-202{\cdot}65\) kJ per mole, negative because the reaction is spontaneous; the WORK the cell can do is the positive of that.

EQUILIBRIUM CONSTANT:
\(\log K_c = \dfrac{n\,E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}}{0{\cdot}059} = \dfrac{2 \times 1{\cdot}05}{0{\cdot}059}\)
\(\log K_c = 35{\cdot}6\)

A value that large — \(K_c \approx 10^{35{\cdot}6}\) — means the reaction goes essentially to completion, which is what a cell potential of over a volt implies.
